body_text: tests/test-license.py builds absolute directory strings with a hard-coded slash suffix. On Windows, glob returns backslash paths, so the intended contrib/linux-kernel/test/include exclusion does not match and the license test reports xxhash.h and unaligned.h as failures. Reproduced on the dev branch with Python 3.13; using os.sep for the suffix makes the same test pass while preserving POSIX behavior. The focused fix is in PR branch codex/fix-license-test-windows.

body_text:
Since #4357 the cmake build enables C++ only for the tests, but `AddZstdCompilationFlags.cmake` still depends on it. For MinGW targets configure fails as soon as `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` is set, which is what cross toolchain files usually do.

Tested on 01b7154f1172432f8abe9b3bb9909e14a1176b7d. Works fine on the latest release (v1.5.7).

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
cmake -S build/cmake -B out \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Windows \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++
```

```
CMake Error at /usr/share/cmake-4.2/Modules/Internal/CheckFlagCommonConfig.cmake:72 (message):
  check_compiler_flag: CXX: needs to be enabled before use.
```

The same command works without `-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` or with `-DZSTD_BUILD_TESTS=ON`. The first commit that fails is 769723aee2.

### Cause

`EnableCompilerFlag()` checks C++ flags when `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` is set, which does not tell whether the language is enabled:

```cmake
if (_CXX AND CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER)
    CHECK_CXX_COMPILER_FLAG(${_flag} CXX_FLAG_${varname})
```

`_CXX` is always true here. `ADD_ZSTD_COMPILATION_FLAGS` passes `_C _CXX` on without `${}`, so the function gets the string `_CXX` and not the value of `ZSTD_ENABLE_CXX`.

### Also affects native compilation

Default build silently loses all flags and the assembly. The block is guarded by `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang"`, which is empty without C++, and `ZSTD_HAS_NOEXECSTACK` needs `CXX_FLAG_WA_NOEXECSTACK`. On x86-64 Linux with gcc 15.2.0:

```
$ cmake -S build/cmake -B out
$ grep C_FLAGS out/lib/CMakeFiles/libzstd_static.dir/flags.make
C_FLAGS = -O3 -DNDEBUG -fPIC -DZSTD_DISABLE_ASM

$ cmake -S build/cmake -B out2 -DZSTD_BUILD_TESTS=ON
$ grep C_FLAGS out2/lib/CMakeFiles/libzstd_static.dir/flags.make
C_FLAGS =  -Wall -Wextra -Wundef -Wshadow -Wcast-align -Wcast-qual -Wstrict-prototypes -Wa,--noexecstack -O3 -DNDEBUG -fPIC
```

### Possible fix

Use `CMAKE_C_COMPILER_ID` for the guard, check C++ flags only if `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LOADED` is set, and do not require `CXX_FLAG_WA_NOEXECSTACK` when C++ is not enabled.

For MinGW targets configure fails as soon as `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` is set, which is what cross toolchain files usually do.

Tested on 01b7154f1172432f8abe9b3bb9909e14a1176b7d. Works fine on the latest release (v1.5.7).

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
cmake -S build/cmake -B out \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Windows \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++
```

```
CMake Error at /usr/share/cmake-4.2/Modules/Internal/CheckFlagCommonConfig.cmake:72 (message):
  check_compiler_flag: CXX: needs to be enabled before use.
```

The same command works without `-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` or with `-DZSTD_BUILD_TESTS=ON`. The first commit that fails is 769723aee2.

### Cause

`EnableCompilerFlag()` checks C++ flags when `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` is set, which does not tell whether the language is enabled:

```cmake
if (_CXX AND CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER)
    CHECK_CXX_COMPILER_FLAG(${_flag} CXX_FLAG_${varname})
```

`_CXX` is always true here. `ADD_ZSTD_COMPILATION_FLAGS` passes `_C _CXX` on without `${}`, so the function gets the string `_CXX` and not the value of `ZSTD_ENABLE_CXX`.

### Also affects native compilation

Default build silently loses all flags and the assembly. The block is guarded by `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang"`, which is empty without C++, and `ZSTD_HAS_NOEXECSTACK` needs `CXX_FLAG_WA_NOEXECSTACK`. On x86-64 Linux with gcc 15.2.0:

```
$ cmake -S build/cmake -B out
$ grep C_FLAGS out/lib/CMakeFiles/libzstd_static.dir/flags.make
C_FLAGS = -O3 -DNDEBUG -fPIC -DZSTD_DISABLE_ASM

$ cmake -S build/cmake -B out2 -DZSTD_BUILD_TESTS=ON
$ grep C_FLAGS out2/lib/CMakeFiles/libzstd_static.dir/flags.make
C_FLAGS =  -Wall -Wextra -Wundef -Wshadow -Wcast-align -Wcast-qual -Wstrict-prototypes -Wa,--noexecstack -O3 -DNDEBUG -fPIC
```

### Possible fix

Use `CMAKE_C_COMPILER_ID` for the guard, check C++ flags only if `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LOADED` is set, and do not require `CXX_FLAG_WA_NOEXECSTACK` when C++ is not enabled.

```sh
#!/usr/local/bin/bash -ex
export PATH="$PWD/prefix/bin:$PATH"
NPROC=$(nproc || echo 6)
ROOTDIR="$PWD"
TARGET="powerpc64le-unknown-freebsd15.0"
PREFIX="$ROOTDIR/prefix"
SYSROOT="$ROOTDIR/sysroot/$TARGET"
FREEBSD_ARCH=powerpc/powerpc64le
CMAKE_ARCH=ppc64le
mkdir -p "$PREFIX"
install_freebsd_sysroot() {
    VERSION="15.1-RELEASE"
    FTPSITE="https://download.freebsd.org/ftp"
    mkdir -p "$SYSROOT"
    [ -f "$SYSROOT/base.txz" ] || wget -O "$SYSROOT/base.txz" "$FTPSITE/releases/$FREEBSD_ARCH/$VERSION/base.txz"
    [ -d "$SYSROOT/usr" ] || tar -C "$SYSROOT" -xvzf "$SYSROOT/base.txz"
}
build_hosted_binutils_gdb() {
    BUILDDIR="$ROOTDIR/build/$TARGET-binutils-gdb"
    SRCDIR="$ROOTDIR/binutils-gdb"
    CONFIGURE_FLAGS=(
        --prefix="$PREFIX"
        --target="$TARGET"
        --without-libiconv-prefix
        --with-sysroot="$SYSROOT"
        --enable-threads=posix
        --disable-werror
        --disable-intl
        --disable-nls
    )
    [ -d "$SRCDIR" ] || git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/gnutools/binutils-gdb.git "$SRCDIR"
    mkdir -p "$BUILDDIR"
    cd "$BUILDDIR"
    [ -f "$BUILDDIR/Makefile" ] || "$SRCDIR/configure" "${CONFIGURE_FLAGS[@]}"
    gmake -j $NPROC
    which -- "${TARGET}-as" || {
        gmake install
    }
    cd ..
}
build_hosted_gcc() {
    BUILDDIR="$ROOTDIR/build/$TARGET-gcc"
    SRCDIR="$ROOTDIR/gcc"
    CONFIGURE_FLAGS=(
        --prefix="$PREFIX"
        --target="$TARGET"
        --with-sysroot="$SYSROOT"
        --with-abi=elfv2
        --enable-gnu-indirect-function
        --enable-initfini-array
        --with-system-zlib
        --without-zstd
        --enable-libstdcxx-threads=yes
        --enable-languages=c,c++
        --enable-threads=posix
        --disable-multilib
        --disable-gnu-unique-object
        --disable-libsanitizer
        --disable-libquadmath
        --disable-bootstrap
        --disable-checking
        --disable-libgomp
        --disable-libssp
        --disable-libvtv
        --disable-shared
        --disable-gcov
        --disable-lto
        --disable-cet
        --disable-nls
    )
    which -- "${TARGET}-as"
    [ -d "$SRCDIR" ] || git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc "$SRCDIR"
    mkdir -p "$BUILDDIR"
    cd "$BUILDDIR"
    [ -f "$BUILDDIR/Makefile" ] || "$SRCDIR/configure" "${CONFIGURE_FLAGS[@]}"
    gmake all-gcc -j $NPROC
    gmake all-target-libgcc -j $NPROC
    gmake all-target-libstdc++-v3 -j $NPROC
    which -- "${TARGET}-gcc" || {
        gmake install-gcc -j $NPROC
        gmake install-target-libgcc -j $NPROC
        gmake install-target-libstdc++-v3 -j $NPROC
    }
    cd ..
}

generate_cmake_toolchain_file() {
    FILE="$ROOTDIR/$TARGET-toolchain.cmake"
    [ -f "$FILE" ] || cat << EOF >"$FILE"
set(CMAKE_SYSROOT "$SYSROOT")
set(CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH "$SYSROOT")
set(CMAKE_STAGING_PREFIX "$PREFIX")
set(PKG_CONFIG_EXECUTABLE "$ROOTDIR/pkg-config")
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME "FreeBSD")
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR "$CMAKE_ARCH")
set(CMAKE_C_COMPILER $PREFIX/bin/$TARGET-gcc)
set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER $PREFIX/bin/$TARGET-g++)
set(CMAKE_ASM_COMPILER $PREFIX/bin/$TARGET-gcc)
set(CMAKE_LINKER $PREFIX/bin/$TARGET-g++)
set(CMAKE_C_FLAGS "")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "")
set(CMAKE_C_HOST_COMPILER clang)
set(CMAKE_CXX_HOST_COMPILER clang++)
set(CMAKE_ASM_HOST_COMPILER clang)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PROGRAM NEVER)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY ONLY)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_INCLUDE ONLY)
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PACKAGE ONLY)
EOF
}
install_freebsd_sysroot
mkdir -p "$ROOTDIR/build"
build_hosted_binutils_gdb
build_hosted_gcc
generate_cmake_toolchain_file
cd "$ROOTDIR"
[ -d zstd ] || git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/facebook/zstd
cd zstd/build/cmake
cmake -S . -B build-cmake \
    -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$ROOTDIR/$TARGET-toolchain.cmake" \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DZSTD_BUILD_SHARED=OFF
cmake --build build-cmake -- -j$NPROC
```

Hi, and thanks for zstd!

While reviewing support for Rust's global allocator in [zstd-rs](https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/pull/373), we ran into a context-copying problem with custom allocators in zstd 1.5.7.

Our wrapper currently implements cloning by creating a destination context with `ZSTD_createCCtx()` or `ZSTD_createDCtx()`, then calling `ZSTD_copyCCtx()` or `ZSTD_copyDCtx()`. If the source was created with a custom allocator, the copy overwrites the destination's `customMem` with the source's callbacks. The destination context itself was allocated through the default allocator, so freeing it then calls the wrong deallocator.

For example, this sequence reproduces an invalid free when `customMem` uses an allocation scheme incompatible with plain `malloc`/`free`:

```c
ZSTD_DCtx* src = ZSTD_createDCtx_advanced(customMem);
ZSTD_DCtx* dst = ZSTD_createDCtx();
ZSTD_copyDCtx(dst, src);
ZSTD_freeDCtx(dst); /* uses src's callbacks for the default-allocated dst */
ZSTD_freeDCtx(src);
```

With our Rust allocation callbacks, which store allocation metadata before the returned pointer, the equivalent Rust sequence aborts with `free(): invalid size`. `ZSTD_copyCCtx()` also copies `customMem`, so an initialized compression context has the same allocator-mismatch concern.

Since contexts are opaque and already store their allocator internally, is there a supported way to copy them safely without also tracking the allocator in the wrapper? Any of these would help:

* A getter returning a context's `ZSTD_customMem`, allowing us to create the destination with the source's allocator.
* A clone function that allocates and copies a context using the source's allocator.
* A copy function that preserves the destination's allocator throughout the copy, including workspace allocations.

The corresponding support for both `CCtx` and `DCtx` would be useful.

I saw [the API evolution plan](https://github.com/facebook/zstd/issues/3390), which deprecates these copy functions and plans their removal. If extending them is not appropriate, what replacement would you recommend for this use case? We'd also appreciate clarification of the allocator compatibility requirements for the existing copy functions.



**AI disclosure:** OpenAI Codex was used to investigate the allocator-copy behavior, run a Rust reproducer against zstd 1.5.7, and draft and submit this issue at my request.

Currently on large corpuses (`-r` with large of many files) zstd's benchmark mode (`-b`) can reasonably look like it got stuck:

- first it ingests the corpus, printing the name of each file
- then nothing happens (it kinda looks stuck on the last direntry) until the first compression level completes
- same for second
- ...

Would be nice if the command-line harness provided some signs of life and some progress e.g. `[N/K] [ xy%]` where K is the number of levels in the benchmark (in -b/-e mode), `N` is the currenth, and xy% is the progress for the current. `-S` exists but it's a bit *too* detailed.

body_text:
**Describe the bug**
On Windows, the CLI's protection against writing the output over the input only compares the two path strings.
`UTIL_isSameFile()` (`programs/util.c`) falls back to `strcmp()` under `_WIN32`, so any other spelling of the same
file passes: different letter case, a `.\` prefix, `/` instead of `\`, a relative against an absolute path, an 8.3
short name, or a hard link.  `FIO_openDstFile()` then opens the "output" with `O_TRUNC`, which empties the input
before a byte of it has been read.  The source was opened with `fopen("rb")`, whose sharing mode allows the second
open for writing, so nothing stops it.

The input is destroyed even though zstd reports an error.  With `--rm` the error at least prevents the removal, but
the data is already gone.

**To Reproduce** (Windows 11, `cmd` or PowerShell)
```
> zstd -V
*** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.7, by Yann Collet ***
> dir a.bin
          30,000 a.bin
> zstd -f a.bin -o A.bin
zstd: error 11 : Src size is incorrect
> dir a.bin
               0 a.bin
```
The same happens with `zstd -f a.bin -o ./a.bin` (tested), and by the same code path with `.\a.bin`, an
absolute path or a short name.  Decompression (`-d`) opens its output through the same `FIO_openDstFile()`.

**Expected behavior**
zstd refuses, as it does for `zstd -f a.bin -o a.bin`: "Refusing to open an output file which will overwrite the
input file".

**Suggested fix**
Compare file identity, not names, on Windows: open both paths (or use the already-open source handle) and compare
`GetFileInformationByHandle()`'s `dwVolumeSerialNumber` + `nFileIndexHigh/Low` (or
`GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileIdInfo)` for ReFS).  That covers case, spelling, short names and hard links.  The
POSIX branch already does the equivalent with `st_dev`/`st_ino`.

**Desktop**
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (26200), x64
- Version: v1.5.7; the same code is unchanged on `dev` (2026-10-05)
- Compiler: MSVC 14.51 (Visual Studio 2026 Build Tools), Release
- Build system: `build/cmake`, Visual Studio generator

**Additional context**
Related Windows-only gaps in the same area (separate issues): `-r` follows directory junctions, and
`--output-dir-flat` collisions are only warned about.

**Environment caveats**
- Found by code review, then reproduced as shown on **Windows 11 only** (x64), with `zstd.exe` built from the v1.5.7 source by **MSVC 14.51** (Visual Studio 2026 Build Tools) through `build/cmake`, **Win64 Release only**.  Not tested with MinGW, clang-cl or the official release binaries, nor on Win32.
- `tests/playTests.sh` was not run (no POSIX shell environment here).
- The functions cited were compared with `dev` (2026-10-05) by source and are unchanged, but `dev` itself was not built.
- The analysis was AI-assisted (Claude); every behaviour reported above was reproduced as shown.

body_text:
**Describe the bug**
On Windows, recursive mode ignores reparse points.  `UTIL_isLink()` (`programs/util.c`) returns 0 on every
non-POSIX platform, and the Windows `UTIL_prepareFileList()` never checks `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`, so a
directory junction or directory symlink inside the tree is entered like an ordinary folder.  Unlike the POSIX
build, `--no-follow`-style behaviour (`followLinks = 0`, the default for `-r`) has no effect.

Consequences:
- `zstd -r --rm folder` compresses **and deletes** files that are not under `folder` at all.
- A junction pointing at an ancestor recurses until the path length or the stack gives out.

**To Reproduce** (Windows 11, `cmd`; `mklink /J` needs no administrator rights)
```
> mkdir outside tree
> echo outside the tree> outside\secret.txt
> echo inside> tree\a.txt
> mklink /J tree\link outside
Junction created for tree\link <<===>> outside
> zstd -r --rm -q tree
> dir /s /b outside tree
...\outside\secret.txt.zst
...\tree\a.txt.zst
```
`outside\secret.txt` has been compressed and deleted, although only `tree` was named.

**Expected behavior**
As on POSIX with the default `followLinks = 0`: junctions and directory symlinks met during recursion are skipped
(with a message at a suitable display level).

**Suggested fix**
In the Windows `UTIL_prepareFileList()`, skip entries whose `cFile.dwFileAttributes` include
`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT` when `followLinks` is 0, and make `UTIL_isLink()` test that attribute
(`GetFileAttributesA`) on Windows.  (`-f` sets `followLinks = 1`, as on POSIX; the reproduction above does not use
`-f`.)

On Windows, recursive mode ignores reparse points.  `UTIL_isLink()` (`programs/util.c`) returns 0 on every
non-POSIX platform, and the Windows `UTIL_prepareFileList()` never checks `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`, so a
directory junction or directory symlink inside the tree is entered like an ordinary folder.  Unlike the POSIX
build, `--no-follow`-style behaviour (`followLinks = 0`, the default for `-r`) has no effect.

Consequences:
- `zstd -r --rm folder` compresses **and deletes** files that are not under `folder` at all.
- A junction pointing at an ancestor recurses until the path length or the stack gives out.

**To Reproduce** (Windows 11, `cmd`; `mklink /J` needs no administrator rights)
```
> mkdir outside tree
> echo outside the tree> outside\secret.txt
> echo inside> tree\a.txt
> mklink /J tree\link outside
Junction created for tree\link <<===>> outside
> zstd -r --rm -q tree
> dir /s /b outside tree
...\outside\secret.txt.zst
...\tree\a.txt.zst
```
`outside\secret.txt` has been compressed and deleted, although only `tree` was named.

**Expected behavior**
As on POSIX with the default `followLinks = 0`: junctions and directory symlinks met during recursion are skipped
(with a message at a suitable display level).

In the Windows `UTIL_prepareFileList()`, skip entries whose `cFile.dwFileAttributes` include

**Describe the bug**
When two inputs map to the same name in the `--output-dir-flat` folder, `FIO_checkFilenameCollisions()`
(`programs/fileio.c`) only prints a warning, and only at display level 2 or above.  zstd then compresses both; the
second output overwrites the first (with `-f`), `--rm` removes both sources, and the exit code is 0.  The first input
is lost.

On Windows it is worse, because the check itself misses collisions:
- it compares names case-sensitively, while the file system is not (`d1\a.txt` and `d2\A.txt` produce the same
  output file and no warning at all);
- it splits paths only on `PATH_SEP` (`\` on Windows), while the output name builder also accepts `/`, so paths
  written with `/` are compared whole and never collide.

**To Reproduce** (Windows 11; the first case also applies on any platform)
```
> mkdir d1 d2 out
> echo first file, d1> d1\x.txt
> echo second file, d2> d2\x.txt
> zstd -f --rm --output-dir-flat out d1\x.txt d2\x.txt
WARNING: Two files have same filename: x.txt
  2 files compressed : ...
> echo %errorlevel%
0
> dir /s /b d1 d2 out
...\out\x.txt.zst          (contains only "second file, d2"; d1\x.txt and d2\x.txt are gone)
```
Case-only difference, no warning:
```
> echo first file, d1> d1\a.txt
> echo second file, d2> d2\A.txt
> zstd -f --rm --output-dir-flat out d1\a.txt d2\A.txt
  2 files compressed : ...
> dir /s /b d1 d2 out
...\out\A.txt.zst          (contains "second file, d2"; both sources deleted)
```

**Expected behavior**
A collision in the flat output folder is an error before anything is written or removed (or at least, `--rm` is
refused for a run that has collisions), and the exit code is non-zero.  On Windows the comparison ignores case and
treats `/` and `\` alike.

**Desktop**
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (26200), x64
- Version: v1.5.7; `FIO_checkFilenameCollisions()` unchanged on `dev` (2026-10-05)
- Compiler: MSVC 14.51 (Visual Studio 2026 Build Tools), Release
- Build system: `build/cmake`, Visual Studio generator

**Environment caveats**
- Found by code review, then reproduced as shown on **Windows 11 only** (x64), with `zstd.exe` built from the v1.5.7 source by **MSVC 14.51** (Visual Studio 2026 Build Tools) through `build/cmake`, **Win64 Release only**.  Not tested with MinGW, clang-cl or the official release binaries, nor on Win32.
- `tests/playTests.sh` was not run (no POSIX shell environment here).
- The functions cited were compared with `dev` (2026-10-05) by source and are unchanged, but `dev` itself was not built.
- The analysis was AI-assisted (Claude); every behaviour reported above was reproduced as shown.

### Issue

I noticed that investigating and fixing security issues can be a significant burden for maintainers.

Following the posts of [Ulises Gascón](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ulisesgascon/), I can see that despite the noise of false positives, a significant number of reported issues are legitimate.

Some lead maintainers (cc @Eomm @mcollina) may also be able to get access through OSS programs:

* https://openai.com/form/codex-for-oss/

### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure the bug has not already been reported


### Fastify version

5.12.5

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

v26.8.2

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

Archlinux

### Description

If a route has a schema, and that schema defines specific content-types (ie, not the catch-all schema if you just do `{ body: { type: ... }}`), then if you:
* do a PUT request (probably also on POST/PATCH but didn't test this)
* without the Content-Type header
* also without the body

then it 'passes' validation and gets into the route handler. this creates a really strange situation where you have to start checking for `undefined`, even if according to the typing it can never be undefined at that point (I can't figure out what exactly causes it to choose strong typing vs `unknown`, but it's not super relevant right now)

if you clone the MRE repo, `npm ci`, `npm start` and look at the logs for request 3, 4, 5 + 6 (the first two are for a different issue, ignore those here):
* no content type but it has a body = 415 (seems fine to me)
* content type but it doesn't have a body = 400 (also seems fine to me)
* no content type and also no body = it gets into the route handler with `body: undefined` which I'm not sure how it does that from the schema

bizarrely, if you just use the catch-all then it will 4xx on that last one, but not if you use content types, and I'm not sure why. The [documentation](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/Reference/Validation-and-Serialization/#body-content-type-validation) does have a warning about needing to define for all content types, but the weird split between `application/json` and `text/plain` in the MRE is the only way I've ever been able to have `application/json` requests also allow booleans, strings, numbers etc, which the catch-all doesn't handle (you get errors about it needing to match exactly one of oneOf, and even if you send `"true"` it will still coerce it to a boolean)

it has been like this since at least 5.8.0 (I didn't test with older versions. it's possible this issue is a "duplicate" of 6597, I didn't put the `#` in front of it because that was labeled as AI spam)

### Link to code that reproduces the bug

https://github.com/barbeque-squared/fastify-body-undefined

### Expected Behavior

The request is rejected, probably with a 400 or 415. If it is intended behaviour, could we get an example schema of how we can still catch this case, because currently, this is creating places in production codebases where something that according to typescript can absolutely never be `undefined` turns out to be `undefined` after all

### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure it has not already been reported

### Fastify version

5.12.5

### Node.js version

v26.7.0

### Operating system

macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64)

### Description

`fastify.close()` resolves, and `onClose` hooks run, while a request is still executing — when the
request arrived on the secondary listener created by the default dual-stack `listen({ port })`.

The documented lifecycle in `docs/Reference/Server.md` says that at step 5 "`onClose` hooks execute.
All in-flight requests have completed and the server is no longer listening", and the Hooks
reference calls `onClose` "the safe place for plugins to release resources such as database
connection pools". Neither holds here.

### Relationship to #4098

This looks similar to #4098 and has a different cause. That one was traced to a Node bug, fixed in
Node 18.7.0 by nodejs/node#43890. This reproduces on Node v26.7.0 and is conditional on the bind:
with `host: '0.0.0.0'` the identical script on the identical Node drains correctly, which points at
Fastify's dual-stack path rather than at Node's idle-socket accounting.

### Steps to Reproduce

```js
import Fastify from 'fastify'

const app = Fastify()
let inFlight = 0

app.addHook('onClose', async () => console.log('onClose fired, inFlight =', inFlight))

app.get('/slow', async () => {
  inFlight++
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000))
  inFlight--
  return { ok: true }
})

await app.listen({ port: 3000 })            // default dual-stack bind

fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/slow')         // arrives over IPv4

setTimeout(async () => {
  const t = Date.now()
```

explicit host. Bare `node:http`, Express and Hono all report `1` and wait.

```js
  // We swallow any error from the secondary server
```

### Fastify version

5.12.5 — source inspected; resolves find-my-way 9.9.0 in our lockfile.

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

24.19.0

### Operating system

macOS

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

27.0.1

### Description

Fastify’s [maxParamLength documentation](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/Reference/Server/#maxparamlength) explicitly describes the option as useful for regex-based routes, “protecting you against ReDoS attacks.”
However, in find-my-way 9.9.0, the route regex executes before the parameter length is checked:
1. [currentNode.regex.exec(param) executes on the parameter](https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/blob/v9.9.0/index.js#L695-L710).
2. [The captured parameter lengths are checked against maxParamLength afterwards](https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/blob/v9.9.0/index.js#L712-L719).
3. If the regex does not match, execution leaves that branch before reaching the length check.

Consequently, maxParamLength restricts captured parameter values but does not bound the input processed by a regex route. An over-limit input can still be processed by the regex, including the failed-match path relevant to excessive backtracking.

### Link to code that reproduces the bug

NA

### Expected Behavior

The documented ReDoS protection should prevent over-limit input from undergoing potentially expensive route regex evaluation, **or** the documentation should clearly explain the protection’s limitations or just not provide false assurances.

### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure the feature has not already been requested


### 🚀 Feature Proposal

The existing `preClose` hook already gives plugins an early point in Fastify's shutdown lifecycle, before the HTTP server has finished draining.

One pattern that might be useful to document is using it to stop a plugin from starting new optional background work once shutdown has begun.

For example, a plugin could keep its own local flag:

```js
let closing = false

fastify.addHook('preClose', async () => {
  closing = true
})

async function startOptionalWork () {
  if (closing) return

  // start work
}
```

I checked this against commit:

`19d5be0daf1c0daace758efe3ea788f924ca1224`

This isn't a request for a new `isClosing` API or access to internal Fastify state. The existing hook seems sufficient; the missing part is just a small example of the pattern.

It would be useful for the documentation to make two boundaries clear.

First, this only prevents new work from starting. Anything already running still needs its own cancellation or completion mechanism.

Second, a flag owned by one plugin instance is local to that instance. If several plugins need to share the same shutdown policy, that state should have an explicitly shared owner rather than implying that local plugin state is automatically shared across scopes.

A small lifecycle test for the example could start `close()`, hold cleanup at a controlled point, verify that no new optional work starts after `preClose`, then release cleanup and let shutdown finish.

I also think it's worth distinguishing this from load-balancer draining.

If an application needs a window where it first withdraws readiness, waits for that change to propagate, and only then calls `fastify.close()`, that still needs to happen outside this pattern. A `preClose` flag only applies once Fastify shutdown has already started.

This shouldn't change hook ordering, `return503OnClosing`, or any other shutdown behavior. It's just documenting how plugins can use the existing lifecycle hook to stop accepting new optional work while handling already-running work separately.

If the current documentation already shows this pattern somewhere, a pointer to it would solve the problem as well.

### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure the bug has not already been reported

### Fastify version

6.0.0-alpha.5 (current `main`); the same `headRouteOnSendHandler` logic also ships on the 5.x line.

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

24.18.0

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

11

### Description

#### Summary

Fastify auto-exposes a `HEAD` route for every `GET` route, and a handler may return a web `Response`. When a `GET` handler returns a `Response`, a `HEAD` request to that route responds **500**, even though the same route responds **200** to `GET`.

This is the same class of bug as #6371 (fixed in #6372 for a web **stream**), but for a web **`Response`** — which is not a `ReadableStream`, so the `getReader` guard added in #6372 does not cover it.

#### Steps to Reproduce

```js
const Fastify = require('fastify')

async function main () {
  const app = Fastify()
  app.get('/', (req, reply) => {
    reply.send(new Response('hello world', {
      status: 200,
      headers: { 'x-demo': 'yes', 'content-type': 'text/plain' }
    }))
  })

  const get = await app.inject({ method: 'GET', path: '/' })
  const head = await app.inject({ method: 'HEAD', path: '/' })
  console.log('GET ', get.statusCode)   // 200
  console.log('HEAD', head.statusCode)  // 500
  await app.close()
}

main()
```

#### Error Details

```
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "string" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or ArrayBuffer. Received an instance of Response
    at Function.byteLength (node:buffer)
    at headRouteOnSendHandler (lib/head-route.js)
```

#### Analysis

`headRouteOnSendHandler` runs in the `onSend` phase, **before** `reply.js` unwraps the `Response`, so it receives the raw `Response` object. That object matches neither the node-stream guard (`payload.resume`) nor the web-stream guard (`payload.getReader`, added in #6372), so it falls through to `Buffer.byteLength(payload)` in `lib/head-route.js`, which throws on a `Response`.

Found while reviewing the auto-HEAD payload handling after #6372, checking whether the other supported web return type — `Response` — was covered. It isn't.

### Expected Behavior

A `HEAD` request to a route whose `GET` handler returns a `Response` should mirror the `GET`: the same status and headers, with an empty body — not a 500. (Same HTTP-spec reasoning as #6371: the `HEAD` response must carry the same headers the corresponding `GET` would send.)

### Link to code that reproduces the bug

Inline minimal reproduction above (Node >= 20, any OS).

body_text:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I subscribe tokens to topics and wanted to handle the token-related failures (mainly cleaning up stale tokens). This was harder than I expected, because `TopicManagementResponse.Error` only exposes a string (`getReason()`), and the possible values come from several different places:

- The values aren't documented. The Javadoc only says the reason is a non-null, non-empty string.
- Since 9.11.0 (#1240), `subscribeToTopic()` uses the FCM v1 API, while the `*Legacy()` methods still use Instance ID error codes. So a stale token can be reported as `registration-token-not-registered` (from `NOT_FOUND`) or as `unregistered` (from `MessagingErrorCode.UNREGISTERED`).
- The fallback uses `toLowerCase()` with the default locale, so with `tr-TR`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` becomes `ınvalıd-argument`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A non-breaking addition:

- A new enum `TopicManagementErrorCode` (e.g. `REGISTRATION_TOKEN_NOT_REGISTERED`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `TOO_MANY_TOPICS`, ..., `UNKNOWN`).
- `TopicManagementResponse.Error#getErrorCode()`, mapped from the raw server code so it doesn't depend on the locale. Unrecognized codes return `UNKNOWN`.
- `getReason()` and `toString()` stay as they are.

```java
for (TopicManagementResponse.Error error : response.getErrors()) {
  switch (error.getErrorCode()) {
    case REGISTRATION_TOKEN_NOT_REGISTERED:
      removeToken(tokens.get(error.getIndex()));
      break;
    default:
      logger.warn("Topic subscription failed: {}", error.getReason());
  }
}
```

Open questions:
1. Should `NOT_FOUND` and `UNREGISTERED` both map to `REGISTRATION_TOKEN_NOT_REGISTERED`?
2. Should `getErrorCode()` return `UNKNOWN` or `null` (like `FirebaseMessagingException#getMessagingErrorCode()`)?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Only fixing the locale issue with `toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)`, but that's still string-based.
- Exposing a `FirebaseMessagingException` per error like `SendResponse#getException()`, but the legacy path has no per-token exception.

**Additional context**
Related: #1072, #1073. I have a patch with unit tests ready (existing tests unchanged, `mvn clean test` passes on JDK 8 and 17). Happy to open a PR if this direction sounds okay.

As mentioned in #5702, advanced features for the `flux push artifact` family of CLI commands are left out of the RFC scope, as they entail a specific flag API that applies only to these commands. The RFC discusses only the API fields and controller options that will apply to all the Flux controllers. The purpose of this issue is to close that gap, defining the scope and proposal for those features.

We will essentially capture the useful features already implemented in [`flux-mirror`](https://fluxcd.io/flux/cli-plugins/flux-mirror/config/#hosts) and implement them in the `flux push artifact` commands with a flag API that makes sense for these commands. Those include:

- GitHub/Forgejo Actions OIDC.
- OIDC tokens from environment variables (for the projected GitLab CI token).
- Kubernetes ServiceAccount token for `generic` container registries.
- SPIFFE features.

I will update this issue at some point to discuss the flag API.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

When running `flux build kustomization --ignore-paths <pattern>`, files matching the ignore pattern (e.g. `**/*.enc.yaml` or `**/secrets/*.yaml`) are **not** ignored if they reside in a base directory referenced by an overlay (e.g. `resources: [- ../../base]`) or in subdirectories discovered during multi-directory builds.

Instead, native `kustomize.Build` resolves the relative paths and pulls the supposedly-ignored files into the build output. If these files are encrypted SOPS files or non-standard manifests, the build fails downstream in `ssautil.ReadObjects` with errors like:
```text
✗ kustomize build failed: error unmarshaling JSON: while decoding JSON: Object 'Kind' is missing in ...
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a directory structure with a base and an overlay:
```text
repro/
├── base/
│   ├── configmap.yaml
│   ├── secret.enc.yaml     # File intended to be ignored
│   └── kustomization.yaml
└── overlay/
    └── kustomization.yaml
```

2. Manifest contents:
* `base/configmap.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: my-config
data:
  key: value
```
* `base/secret.enc.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: ENC[AES256_GCM,data:foo]
kind: ENC[AES256_GCM,data:bar]
```
* `base/kustomization.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - ./configmap.yaml
  - ./secret.enc.yaml
```
* `overlay/kustomization.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - ../base
```

3. Run `flux build` on the overlay while explicitly ignoring `*.enc.yaml`:
```bash
flux build kustomization test \
  --path ./overlay \
  --kustomization-file <(echo '
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 1m
  path: ./overlay
  prune: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system
') \
  --ignore-paths "**/*.enc.yaml"
```

**Outcome**:
- Running directly against `./base`: `--ignore-paths "**/*.enc.yaml"` works (it strips `secret.enc.yaml` from `base/kustomization.yaml.resources`).
- Running against `./overlay`: `--ignore-paths "**/*.enc.yaml"` fails. Native Kustomize follows `../base`, reads `secret.enc.yaml`, and outputs it.

### Expected behavior

`--ignore-paths` is documented as taking patterns following `.gitignore` format. Any file matching the ignore pattern across the repository/build tree should be excluded from the build, regardless of whether it is referenced directly in the root `kustomization.yaml` or imported indirectly via `resources: [- ../../base]`.

### OS / Distro

macOS

### Flux version

v2.9.4

### Flux check

```text
► checking prerequisites
✔ Kubernetes 1.36.1-aliyun.1 >=1.33.0-0
► checking controllers
✔ helm-controller: deployment ready
✔ image-automation-controller: deployment ready
✔ image-reflector-controller: deployment ready
✔ kustomize-controller: deployment ready
✔ notification-controller: deployment ready
✔ source-controller: deployment ready
► checking crds
✔ all checks passed
```

### Additional context

#### Root Cause in Code
1. In `fluxcd/flux2/internal/build/build.go`:
```go
ignoreList := strings.Join(b.ignore, "\n")
gen := kustomize.NewGeneratorWithIgnore("", ignoreList, unstructured.Unstructured{Object: data})
buildFS, buildDir, action, er := b.generate(*k, b.resourcesPath)
...
m, err = b.do(ctx, *k, buildFS, buildDir) // Calls kustomize.Build(fs, dirPath)
```
2. In `fluxcd/pkg/kustomize/kustomize_generator.go`:
```go
if g.filter {
    if err := filterKsWithIgnoreFiles(&kus, dirPath, ignorePatterns, ignoreDomain); err != nil {
        return nil, "", action, err
    }
}
```
3. In `fluxcd/pkg/kustomize/filters.go`, `filterSlice` only inspects and mutates the `resources:` and `components:` slices of the single `kustomization.yaml` at the root `dirPath`.
4. Once `kustomize.Build` starts, Kustomize's internal loader directly reads the filesystem. Because the ignore filter was only applied to the root YAML slice and not to the underlying `filesys.FileSystem` wrapper, native Kustomize loads any referenced base directory directly from disk without ignore filtering.

#### Suggested Fix
Instead of only trimming the root `kustypes.Kustomization.Resources` slice in `kustomize_generator.go`, apply the ignore filter at the `filesys.FileSystem` layer (e.g. decorating `filesys.FileSystem` in `inMemoryFsBackend` / `onDiskFsBackend` so that `fs.ReadFile`, `fs.Exists`, and directory walkers treat ignored paths as non-existent).

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

{"repository": "fluxcd/flux2", "task_candidate_id": 4799, "repository_id": 101, "issue_number": 6067, "github_issue_id": 5446893491, "html_url": "https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/issues/6067", "created_at": "2026-09-14T08:14:35+00:00", "author_association": "NONE", "title": "`flux build --ignore-paths` only filters root resources, leaking ignored files in bases and sub-directories", "body_text": "### Describe the bug

When running `flux build kustomization --ignore-paths <pattern>`, files matching the ignore pattern (e.g. `**/*.enc.yaml` or `**/secrets/*.yaml`) are **not** ignored if they reside in a base directory referenced by an overlay (e.g. `resources: [- ../../base]`) or in subdirectories discovered during multi-directory builds.

Instead, native `kustomize.Build` resolves the relative paths and pulls the supposedly-ignored files into the build output. If these files are encrypted SOPS files or non-standard manifests, the build fails downstream in `ssautil.ReadObjects` with errors like:
```text
✗ kustomize build failed: error unmarshaling JSON: while decoding JSON: Object 'Kind' is missing in ...
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a directory structure with a base and an overlay:
```text
repro/
├── base/
│   ├── configmap.yaml
│   ├── secret.enc.yaml     # File intended to be ignored
│   └── kustomization.yaml
└── overlay/
    └── kustomization.yaml
```

2. Manifest contents:
* `base/configmap.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: my-config
data:
  key: value
```
* `base/secret.enc.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: ENC[AES256_GCM,data:foo]
kind: ENC[AES256_GCM,data:bar]
```
* `base/kustomization.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - ./configmap.yaml
  - ./secret.enc.yaml
```
* `overlay/kustomization.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - ../base
```

3. Run `flux build` on the overlay while explicitly ignoring `*.enc.yaml`:
```bash
flux build kustomization test \
  --path ./overlay \
  --kustomization-file <(echo '
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 1m
  path: ./overlay
  prune: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system
') \
  --ignore-paths "**/*.enc.yaml"
```

**Outcome**:
- Running directly against `./base`: `--ignore-paths "**/*.enc.yaml"` works (it strips `secret.enc.yaml` from `base/kustomization.yaml.resources`).
- Running against `./overlay`: `--ignore-paths "**/*.enc.yaml"` fails. Native Kustomize follows `../base`, reads `secret.enc.yaml`, and outputs it.

### Expected behavior

`--ignore-paths` is documented as taking patterns following `.gitignore` format. Any file matching the ignore pattern across the repository/build tree should be excluded from the build, regardless of whether it is referenced directly in the root `kustomization.yaml` or imported indirectly via `resources: [- ../../base]`.

### OS / Distro

macOS

### Flux version

v2.9.4

### Flux check

```text
► checking prerequisites
✔ Kubernetes 1.36.1-aliyun.1 >=1.33.0-0
► checking controllers
✔ helm-controller: deployment ready
✔ image-automation-controller: deployment ready
✔ image-reflector-controller: deployment ready
✔ kustomize-controller: deployment ready
✔ notification-controller: deployment ready
✔ source-controller: deployment ready
► checking crds
✔ all checks passed
```

### Additional context

#### Root Cause in Code
1. In `fluxcd/flux2/internal/build/build.go`:
```go
ignoreList := strings.Join(b.ignore, "\n")
gen := kustomize.NewGeneratorWithIgnore("", ignoreList, unstructured.Unstructured{Object: data})
buildFS, buildDir, action, er := b.generate(*k, b.resourcesPath)
...
m, err = b.do(ctx, *k, buildFS, buildDir) // Calls kustomize.Build(fs, dirPath)
```
2. In `fluxcd/pkg/kustomize/kustomize_generator.go`:
```go
if g.filter {
    if err := filterKsWithIgnoreFiles(&kus, dirPath, ignorePatterns, ignoreDomain); err != nil {
        return nil, "", action, err
    }
}
```
3. In `fluxcd/pkg/kustomize/filters.go`, `filterSlice` only inspects and mutates the `resources:` and `components:` slices of the single `kustomization.yaml` at the root `dirPath`.
4. Once `kustomize.Build` starts, Kustomize's internal loader directly reads the filesystem. Because the ignore filter was only applied to the root YAML slice and not to the underlying `filesys.FileSystem` wrapper, native Kustomize loads any referenced base directory directly from disk without ignore filtering.

#### Suggested Fix
Instead of only trimming the root `kustypes.Kustomization.Resources` slice in `kustomize_generator.go`, apply the ignore filter at the `filesys.FileSystem` layer (e.g. decorating `filesys.FileSystem` in `inMemoryFsBackend` / `onDiskFsBackend` so that `fs.ReadFile`, `fs.Exists`, and directory walkers treat ignored paths as non-existent).

## Problem
As an infra team we'd like to use Flux kustomization patches to enforce some patches on the contents of a synced application. 

`spec.patches` are merged into the package's `kustomization.yaml` and run in the same build, where kustomize always runs patches *before* replacements (and Components run replacements earlier still). So a patch targeting a value the package's `replacements:` also sets gets overwritten.

`spec.postBuild.substitute` runs after the build and does win, but it can't be used to enforce parameter settings, it's rather opt-in from the application author's side.

## Proposal

Add `spec.postBuild.patches`, same shape as `spec.patches`, applied to the rendered output after the build (alongside `substitute`):

```yaml
spec:
  path: ./packages/my-app
  postBuild:
    patches:
      - target: { kind: HelmRelease, name: my-app }
        patch: |
          - op: replace
            path: /spec/targetNamespace
            value: production-ns
```

It could run after replacements have fired, it gets the last word e equivalent of a wrapper kustomization patching the built package as a base, without a separate git dir.

Related: kustomize#4476, kustomize#4060, kustomize-controller#1000, flux2#5664.

body_text:
Flux 2.10.0 promotes the Flux alerting APIs to GA, integrates Flux with SPIFFE, adds tenant provisioning to ArtifactGenerator, atomic reconciles for HelmRelease with OCIRepository charts and GitHub App support for Client ID as an alternative to App ID.

:date: **Target date:** 26 October

🚀  **Roadmap milestone:** https://fluxcd.io/roadmap/#v210-mid-q4-2026

### ℹ️ Highlights

- Promote the `Event`, `Alert` and `Provider` APIs to `notification.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1`
- Introduce `zoom` and `incident.io` notification providers
- [RFC-0014](https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/blob/main/rfcs/0014-advanced-support-for-short-lived-cryptographic-material) SPIFFE mTLS between the Flux controllers
- [RFC-0014](https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/blob/main/rfcs/0014-advanced-support-for-short-lived-cryptographic-material) Kubernetes ServiceAccount tokens and JWT-SVIDs auth for `generic` OCIRepository and ImageRepository
- Tenant namespace provisioning with ArtifactGenerator (discover, create and prune namespaces from source artifacts)
- Atomic reconciles for HelmRelease with OCIRepository charts
- GitHub App support for Client ID as an alternative to App ID

### ⚠️ Deprecations

The following APIs are deprecated and will be removed in a future release:

- `notification.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1beta3`

The [deprecated fields](https://github.com/fluxcd/notification-controller/issues/1144) have been removed in the Alert and Provider `v1` APIs.

### ⚠️ End-of-life support

- Flux v2.7.x
- Kubernetes v1.34.x

### Dependencies updates

- [x] Go 1.27
- [x] Kubernetes 1.37
- [x] Controller Runtime 0.25
- [x] Kustomize 5.8
- [x] Helm 4.3
- [x] Cosign 3.1

### Release checklist

- [x] source-controller v1.10.0
- [x] source-watcher v2.3.0
- [x] kustomize-controller v1.10.0
- [x] notification-controller v1.10.0
- [x] helm-controller v1.7.0
- [x] image-reflector-controller v1.3.0
- [x] image-automation-controller v1.3.0
- [x] flux-benchmark v2.10.0
- [ ] flux2 v2.10.0
- [ ] terraform-provider-flux v1.10.0
- [ ] agent-skills v0.4.0

### Conformance testing

| Distribution | Versions |
|:--------|:--------|
| Kubernetes KinD | 1.35, 1.36, 1.37 |
| OpenShift | 4.21.0-okd |
| K3s | 1.35, 1.36, 1.37 |
| AWS | EKS 1.36 |
| Azure | AKS 1.36 |
| Google Cloud | GKE 1.36 |

### Documentation

- [ ] Publish SPIFFE integration docs
- [ ] Publish ArtifactGenerator tenant provisioning docs
- [ ] Update API docs
- [ ] Publish v2.10 website
- [ ] Publish Flux release change log to GitHub & Slack

We should use `go fix ./...` in CI before the dirty worktree check across all our repos:

https://go.dev/blog/gofix

Requirements:
* `go fix ./...` has to run as part of `make test` together with the other commands that generate things/modify Git-versioned files. This is how our dev workflow works. Without this, the dev would have a surprise when the CI runs.
* This command has to run on every directory containing a `go.mod` inside each repo.
* Each PR must also contain the changes from `go fix`, otherwise the CI will fail the very check introduced by the PR.

- [ ] `flux2`
- [x] `cli-utils`

- [ ] `kustomize-controller`
- [ ] `helm-controller`
- [ ] `notification-controller`
- [ ] `image-reflector-controller`
- [ ] `image-automation-controller`
- [ ] `source-watcher`
- [ ] `terraform-provider-flux`

### Describe the Issue

In the instructions for the 2nd workshop in the Relational Databases course (https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/relational-databases-v9/workshop-database-of-video-game-characters/build-a-database-of-video-game-characters) , the local setup instructions do not say what to do explicitly if you have already completed the instructions for the 1st workshop (https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/relational-databases-v9/workshop-bash-boilerplate/build-a-boilerplate). That is, should the person delete their old rdb-alpha dir for example or should they skip a few steps and start from rebuilding the container? 

### Affected Page

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/relational-databases-v9/workshop-database-of-video-game-characters/build-a-database-of-video-game-characters

### Your code

N/A


### Expected behavior

Instructions need to clarify how people with local setup should start a 2nd workshop after completing the instructions from a prior (first) workshop.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### System

N/A


### Additional context

The instructions may need to be tailored to linux vs wsl2 setups. In wsl2 for example, the only way forward is to create a new rdb-alpha local copy with a new folder name or path or the remaining instructions will not work (user will be returned to the prior workshop rather than allowed to choose a new one)

body_text:
### Describe the Issue

In the [Build a Bookmarks Manager](https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/javascript-v9/lab-bookmark-manager-app/build-a-bookmark-manager-app) lab in the "localStorage and CRUD Operations" section of the JavaScript course, the example project provided in the instructions is not working correctly:

**Problem occurs when:** attempting to add a bookmark in the provided example project. 

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Press "Add Bookmark" (`#add-bookmark-button`) to open form
2. Filling in the "Name" and "URL" inputs in the form
3. Press "Add Bookmark" (`#add-bookmark-button-form`)) to submit form and add bookmark.

**Expected behavior:** It's supposed to add a new bookmark and then clear and close the form. The user should then be able to see the newly added bookmark when pressing "View Category" with the same category selected.

**Actual behavior:** Nothing happens. The form is not closed and the bookmark is not added.

**Suspected reason:** In the browser's DevTools console, the message `SecurityError: Window.localStorage getter: Forbidden in a sandboxed document without the 'allow-same-origin' flag.` appears every time step 3 is repeated. Every time the button is pressed, a copy of the same error message appears in the console.

### Affected Page

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/javascript-v9/lab-bookmark-manager-app/build-a-bookmark-manager-app

### System

Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:156.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/156.0

### Additional context

On the slim chance any of them was somehow having an effect, I tested this both before and after disabling all browser extensions and Firefox's "Enhanced Tracking Protection". Results were identical.

### Describe the Issue

All 15 behavioral tests in Debug an ISBN Validator suppress exceptions raised by `main()`. For example, the test for missing comma-separated values contains:

> ```python
> try:
>   main()
> except:
>   pass
> finally:
>   print = built_in_print
>
> assert "Enter comma-separated values." in out
> ```

Once the expected message has been printed, an unhandled exception does not cause the test to fail. This allows faulty error handling to pass even though the user stories require the program to handle errors without crashing.

To reproduce, start with the supplied solution and append this code, leaving the global `main()` call commented out:

```python
original_main = main

def main():
    original_main()
    raise RuntimeError("unhandled failure")
```

This version passes all challenge tests.

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/lab-isbn-validator/debug-an-isbn-validator

### Expected behavior

The behavioral tests should fail when `main()` raises an unhandled exception, even if it has already printed the expected message. The supplied solution should continue to pass, and test cleanup should restore `print` whether execution succeeds or fails.

Removing the `except` can maybe be the way? Not necessarily in all tests, but at least one, maybe an additional one that verify errors are properly handled?

body_text:
### Describe the Issue

1. **The IDE definition is vague and misses an Oxford comma**
   > `Before you can start building your Python scripts locally, you will need to install a code editor or IDE. IDE stands for Integrated Development Environment and it has features including a code editor, testing tools, a terminal and more.`

   `Integrated development environment` is a common noun, and `and more` does not identify another feature. The list also needs a comma before its final item.

2. **The platform list has punctuation and terminology errors**
   > ``One popular code editor that many developers use is VS Code. Visit `https://code.visualstudio.com/download` to download VS Code which supports Mac, Windows and Linux environments. This is the editor that will be used in this lesson.``

   The nonrestrictive `which` clause needs a comma, the list needs an Oxford comma, and Apple's operating system is named macOS rather than Mac.

3. **The folder instructions are repetitive and under-punctuated**
   > ``Once you have downloaded your editor, you will need to open it. Once it is opened, you will need to open a folder. You can click on the `File` menu option in the upper left hand corner and click on `Open Folder`. From there, you can choose or create a folder for your project. For extra practice outside of the lesson, you might want a folder named `python-projects`.``

   The first two sentences repeat `Once` and `open`, while `upper left hand` needs compound hyphens before `corner`.

4. **The lesson omits the VS Code Python extension**
   > ``One popular code editor that many developers use is VS Code. Visit `https://code.visualstudio.com/download` to download VS Code which supports Mac, Windows and Linux environments. This is the editor that will be used in this lesson.``

   > ``To run this code, you have a few options. The first option is to click on the run button which looks like a play button located in the upper right hand corner. That will open a terminal and run your Python script there. You should see the text `"Hello, world!"`.``

   The `Run Python File` button belongs to Microsoft's Python extension, not to a bare VS Code installation. The learner is told only to install VS Code, so the described button may not be available. See [Python in Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/python#_run-python-code).

5. **The file-creation paragraph has grammar and spelling errors**
   > ``Once you have your folder set up, you can open the explorer which is the left sidebar in VS Code. Click on the `New File` icon which looks like a piece of paper with a plus icon over it. Then create a file called `main.py` and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. The `.py` is a file extension signalling this is a Python file.``

   The two `which` clauses need commas, `signalling` is British spelling, and `The .py is a file extension` is awkward.

### Describe the Issue

The `create-next-challenge` and `insert-challenge` helper scripts both offer the quiz challenge type, but selecting it causes template generation to fail:

> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')`

Their shared `newChallengePrompts` function returns `title`, `dashedName`, and `challengeType`. Neither caller supplies `questionCount` to the quiz template, which reads that property and calls `count.toString()`. The failure occurs before the challenge file is created.

### Affected Pages

These contributor tools are affected rather than a learner page:

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/b187f6b972a1875118711735f2d92b85eecd9ba7/tools/challenge-helper-scripts/create-next-challenge.ts

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/b187f6b972a1875118711735f2d92b85eecd9ba7/tools/challenge-helper-scripts/insert-challenge.ts

### Expected behavior

Selecting the quiz challenge type in either script should prompt the contributor to choose 10 or 20 questions. The script should then create a quiz with the selected number of questions and update the block's challenge order without throwing an exception. Missing or unsupported question counts should be handled before rendering the quiz template.

### Describe the Issue

1. **Search box named incorrectly**

   > `Another alternative is to use the Search File Explorer. You will find it at the top right of the Explorer window, where you can see "Search Documents."`

   The screenshot clearly shows the Documents folder and its matching `Search Documents` placeholder, so that label is valid in this example. The remaining wording problem is `the Search File Explorer`; the control is the search box in File Explorer.

2. **Spotlight settings instructions need a macOS version**

   > `If you don't see this icon on the menu bar, you can add it in the Control Center settings.`
   >
   > `Go to your settings, filter by "Control Center", click on this option and then scroll down until you find the "Spotlight" option.`

   macOS Tahoe 26 uses Menu Bar settings to add the icon, while these instructions and the accompanying screenshot show the older Control Center route without identifying a version. [Apple documents the Tahoe Menu Bar route](https://support.apple.com/en-au/guide/mac-help/mchlp1008/26/mac/26).

3. **Plural noun missing in two questions**

   > `What is the name of a powerful search tool built into macOS that helps you find files and folder in your entire system quickly?`

   > `What is the name of the horizontal bar, typically located at the bottom of a Windows computer screen, where you can search for files and folder?`

   Both questions use "files and folder," mixing plural and singular forms.

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/responsive-web-design-v9/lecture-working-with-file-systems/how-to-search-for-files-and-folders-on-your-computer

### Expected behavior

The File Explorer instructions should identify the control as the search box in File Explorer. Spotlight instructions and screenshots should identify the macOS version they describe, with a usable route for learners on other versions. The prose should follow American-English quotation punctuation, and both questions should use matching plural nouns.

body_text:
### Describe the Issue

The dynamic programming lecture contains three inconsistencies:

1. The introduction presents polynomial running time as a general guarantee:

   > `This approach transforms problems that would normally take exponential time into ones that can be solved in polynomial time.`

   Avoiding repeated calculations does not guarantee polynomial time. The number of distinct subproblems and the work required for each determine the complexity. Numeric dynamic programming tables can also have pseudopolynomial complexity, as explained in these [MIT lecture notes](https://www.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-fall-2011/3484e876d81aba07911a1109f5b5e81e_MIT6_006F11_lec21.pdf).

2. The climbing-stairs explanations refer to a function that the examples never define. For example:

   > ``This implementation has exponential time complexity because of massive redundant calculations. When calculating `climb_stairs(5)`, here's what happens:``

   The same undefined name appears throughout the naive-recursion discussion, the memoization explanation and comparison, and the introduction to the bottom-up trace. The examples define `climb_stairs_recursive`, `climb_stairs_memo`, and `climb_stairs_tabulation`, so the prose does not identify the corresponding implementation.

3. The coin-change example substitutes an incorrect value into its calculation:

   > `# dp[6] = min(dp[5]+1, dp[3]+1, dp[2]+1) = min(3+1, 1+1, 2+1) = 2`

   With denominations `[1, 3, 4]`, amount 5 requires two coins, so `dp[5]` is 2. The substitution uses 3 instead, contradicting the later trace and the executable function. The final minimum is still 2.

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/lecture-understanding-dynamic-programming/what-is-dynamic-programming-and-what-are-some-common-algorithms

### Expected behavior

The introduction should describe polynomial-time improvements as possible for suitable problems, without implying that dynamic programming always guarantees polynomial time.

The climbing-stairs explanations and comparisons should refer to the function names defined in their corresponding examples.

The coin-change calculation should use table values consistent with the executable example and the detailed trace.

Numeric dynamic programming tables can also have pseudopolynomial complexity, as explained in these [MIT lecture notes](https://www.ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-fall-2011/3484e876d81aba07911a1109f5b5e81e_MIT6_006F11_lec21.pdf).

### Describe the Issue

1. **Frontmatter title capitalizes a preposition**

   > `title: How Do Dynamic Arrays Differ From Static Arrays?`

   The title capitalizes `From`, although this preposition should be lowercase.

2. **Incorrect preposition and article**

   > `Their underlying behavior can have an important effect in the program's efficiency, so let's learn about dynamic and static arrays and their differences, so you can choose the most efficient one for your program.`

   > ``Inserting an element at the end of the array takes constant time `O(1)` if there is still space available in the dynamic array, but if the array is full and needs resizing, this operation has a `O(n)` complexity.``

   An effect is on the program's efficiency, not in it. The spoken letter O begins with a vowel sound and takes `an`.

3. **Matching title in block metadata needs the same correction**

   > `"title": "How Do Dynamic Arrays Differ From Static Arrays?"`

   The matching `challengeOrder` title in `curriculum/structure/blocks/lecture-working-with-common-data-structures.json` repeats the lesson title defect described above.

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/lecture-working-with-common-data-structures/how-do-dynamic-arrays-differ-from-static-arrays

### Expected behavior

1. **Lesson title:** The frontmatter title should read `How Do Dynamic Arrays Differ from Static Arrays?`, with the preposition `from` lowercase under the curriculum's title capitalization rules.

2. **Grammar:** The introductory paragraph should describe an effect **on** the program's efficiency. The resizing paragraph should use `an` before `O(n)`, because the spoken letter O starts with a vowel sound. The complexity expression should retain its code formatting.

3. **Block metadata:** The matching `challengeOrder` entry in `curriculum/structure/blocks/lecture-working-with-common-data-structures.json` should also read `How Do Dynamic Arrays Differ from Static Arrays?`, matching the corrected lesson title.

### Describe the Issue

The Media Catalogue workshop contains grammar, punctuation, and instruction-wording errors in the following steps.

1. **Step 21 (`68b80ef5aae8b2078b0a9dc1`)**

   > ``As you can see, `series1` is displayed in the same format of a `Movie` object because it's inheriting its parent's `__str__` method. In the next step, you'll override the `__str__` method to provide a custom string representation.``

   > ``You should not have `print(series1)` in your code``

   The description uses the wrong preposition for a comparison, and the hint is missing its final period.

2. **Step 29 (`68b94e26d2216958479e24bf`)**

   > ``Create an `if` statement that uses `isinstance` to check if `media_item` is an instance of `Movie` and raise a `TypeError` with the message `Only Movie or TVSeries instances can be added`.``

   The instruction tells learners to raise an error for a valid Movie instance. The hints and existing validation require the error only for an item that is not an instance of Movie or its subclasses. The description is missing the negation.

3. **Step 30 (`68b95956da014b1a8e32ffb3`)**

   > ``Create a class named `MediaError`. Make it inherit from the `Exception` class and add to it a docstring saying `Custom exception for media-related errors.`.``

   The sentence ends with two periods, one inside the docstring and one after the closing backtick.

4. **Step 31 (`68b95c952d50ed52abe02ed3`)**

   > ``Inside it, call `super().__init__(message)` to ensure the mechanisms for storing and displaying the error message, which is already present in the `Exception` class, can work properly.``

   The relative clause uses a singular verb for the plural noun mechanisms.

5. **Step 35 (`68b970cf5f000fafa537dbbd`)**

   > ``This kind of messages can be extremely useful when you are trying to debug your code.``

   The singular phrase This kind is paired with the plural noun messages.

6. **Step 38 (`68b995fb1712f635a9387fe8`)**

   > ``Create another method named `get_tv_series` and make it return a list with all the instances of `TVSeries` you can found in `self.items`.``

   The modal verb can is followed by found instead of the base form of the verb.

7. **Step 39 (`68b99699b8d2ab4092ba0623`)**

   > ``After the `if` statement in your `__str__` method, create two variables named `movies` and `series` and assign it a call to the `get_movies` method and a call to the `get_tv_series` method, respectively.``

   > ``You assign `self.get_movies()` to your `movies` variable.``

   > ``You assign `self.get_tv_series()` to your `series` variable.``

   The description refers to two variables with the singular pronoun it. Both assignment hints omit should, unlike the surrounding requirement hints.

8. **Step 42 (`68b99be831fb229c9d950296`)**

   > ``You should have a second `if` statement in your `__str__` method.``

   > ``You should have `result += '=== TV SERIES ===\n'` inside your second `if` statement.``

   > ``You should have a `for` loop in your second `if` statement.``

   All three hints refer to the second conditional, but the requested TV-series conditional is the third. The method already contains the empty-catalogue guard and the movies conditional. The tests check for three conditionals and inspect the one at index 2.

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-21

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-29

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-30

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-31

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-35

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-38

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-39

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-media-catalogue/step-42

### Expected behavior

Descriptions and hints should use correct grammar, agreement, and sentence punctuation. The Step 30 instruction should preserve the period required inside the docstring without duplicating the sentence-ending punctuation. Step 39 should refer to both variables with a plural pronoun and phrase both assignment hints as requirements.

Step 29 should instruct learners to reject items that are not instances of `Movie` or its subclasses, matching the existing hints and validation. All three affected Step 42 hints should identify the TV-series conditional as the third `if` statement in `MediaCatalogue.__str__`.

It is recommended to add a clear explanatory note in the contributor guidelines and search results. This note should clarify which target branch (e.g., main vs staging) new contributors should use when setting up their local environment and submitting Pull Requests, helping avoid confusion for first-time contributors.

### Describe the Issue

In `client/i18n/locales/english/intro.json`, two Python lecture blocks have introductions that repeat their block names without describing what the lessons teach:

1. `lecture-understanding-object-oriented-programming-and-encapsulation`:

   > `Learn about understanding object oriented programming and encapsulation in these lessons.`

2. `lecture-understanding-inheritance-and-polymorphism`:

   > `Learn about understanding inheritance and polymorphism in these lessons.`

Both descriptions use the boilerplate pattern `Learn about <block name> in these lessons.` They give learners no information beyond the title. Removing the word `understanding` would leave that problem intact.

Each block has an entry under `introduction-to-oop-in-python`, `python-v9`, and `python-programming-fundamentals`, so all six descriptions are affected.

The first block's title also uses `Object Oriented Programming` without the hyphen in the compound adjective, in all three entries.

### Affected Lines

`introduction-to-oop-in-python`, object-oriented programming and encapsulation title and description:

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/23079d05dde925ec3330544f74b48cc35e12e898/client/i18n/locales/english/intro.json#L1780-L1784

`introduction-to-oop-in-python`, inheritance and polymorphism description:

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/23079d05dde925ec3330544f74b48cc35e12e898/client/i18n/locales/english/intro.json#L1798-L1802

`python-v9`, object-oriented programming and encapsulation title and description:

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/23079d05dde925ec3330544f74b48cc35e12e898/client/i18n/locales/english/intro.json#L6735-L6739

`python-v9`, inheritance and polymorphism description:

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/23079d05dde925ec3330544f74b48cc35e12e898/client/i18n/locales/english/intro.json#L6753-L6757

`python-programming-fundamentals`, object-oriented programming and encapsulation title and description:

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/23079d05dde925ec3330544f74b48cc35e12e898/client/i18n/locales/english/intro.json#L10729-L10733

`python-programming-fundamentals`, inheritance and polymorphism description:

https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/blob/23079d05dde925ec3330544f74b48cc35e12e898/client/i18n/locales/english/intro.json#L10747-L10751

### Expected behavior

Each block should have a concise description of its lesson content that gives learners useful information beyond the block title:

- The object-oriented programming and encapsulation block should describe its coverage of classes and objects, encapsulation, and getters and setters for accessing and validating attributes.
- The inheritance and polymorphism block should describe its coverage of code reuse through inheritance and polymorphism, and name mangling.

The descriptions should replace the boilerplate with content specific to each block, with the same description used consistently across its three superblock entries. A wording adjustment within the existing boilerplate does not satisfy this change.

The object-oriented programming block's title should also use the correctly hyphenated compound adjective in all three entries.

### Describe the Issue

The Implement the Selection Sort Algorithm lab tests enforce two restrictions missing from the description. Its user stories prohibit `sort()` and `sorted()` and require in-place sorting using swaps, but do not state that module imports and methods that add or remove list elements are prohibited.

The restrictions appear only in the test hints:

> You should not import any module or use built-in sorting methods in your code.

> Your `selection_sort` should modify the input list in-place. You should not use any method adding, or removing items from the list.

Learners should be told these restrictions before encountering failing tests.

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/lab-selection-sort/implement-selection-sort-algorithm

### Expected behavior

A note immediately below the user stories should state that importing modules and using methods that add or remove list elements are prohibited. Use this format:

```md
**Note:** <explanation of the restrictions>
```

### Describe the Issue

The Build a Planet Class lab requires the initializer to store the supplied values:

> Assigns the values passed in to the instance attributes `name`, `planet_type`, and `star`.

However, the three attribute tests inspect the source using `_Node` and require these individual assignment expressions:

> `assert init.find_variable('self.name').is_equivalent('self.name = name')`
>
> `assert init.find_variable('self.planet_type').is_equivalent('self.planet_type = planet_type')`
>
> `assert init.find_variable('self.star').is_equivalent('self.star = star')`

A tuple assignment satisfies the user story but fails all three tests:

```python
self.name, self.planet_type, self.star = name, planet_type, star
```

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/lab-planet-class/build-a-planet-class

### Expected behavior

The three attribute tests should check the values stored on instantiated `Planet` objects instead of requiring specific assignment syntax. Separate assignments and tuple assignment should both pass when they store the supplied values correctly.

Keep the current three hints and their separate tests. Each test should create two instances with different values for all three constructor arguments, then check its corresponding attribute on both instances. Creating both instances before checking either verifies that the first instance retains its values after the second is constructed. Distinct inputs also catch hardcoded attribute values.

### Describe the Issue

Step 24 of the discount calculator workshop introduces `DiscountEngine.calculate_best_price` with these instructions:

> ``Now create a method named `calculate_best_price` in your `DiscountEngine` class. This method should take `self`, `product`, and `user_tier` as parameters, and return a `float`.``

The parameter test requires `product: Product` and `user_tier: str`, but the instructions do not specify these annotations. For example, this method has the requested parameters, the expected return annotation, and the requested placeholder body, but fails the parameter test:

```py
def calculate_best_price(self, product, user_tier) -> float:
    pass
```

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-discount-calculator/step-24

### Expected behavior

The instructions should explicitly specify the required `Product` annotation for `product` and `str` annotation for `user_tier`. They should also clearly describe `float` as the return type annotation while the method body remains `pass`.

### Describe the Issue

The Shortest Path Algorithm workshop repeats instructions to use `pass` in empty bodies. Learners have already learned this in the first Python module, so these reminders add unnecessary wording at this point in the curriculum.

1. Step 3, when defining `shortest_path`:

   > ``Add a `pass` statement inside the function body for now.``

2. Step 11, when adding the inner loop:

   > ``The loop should iterate through each `node_no` in `range(n)`, where `n` is the number of nodes in the graph. Add `pass` as the body of the loop for now.``

3. Step 12, when adding the conditional:

   > ``Add `pass` as a placeholder inside the conditional block.``

4. Step 21, when iterating over the target nodes:

   > ``Add a `for` loop that iterates through each `node_no` in the `targets` iterable. Add `pass` as a placeholder inside the loop body.``

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-shortest-path-algorithm/step-3

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-shortest-path-algorithm/step-11

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-shortest-path-algorithm/step-12

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/workshop-shortest-path-algorithm/step-21

### Expected behavior

These descriptions should explain the function, loops, and conditional to create without reminding learners to fill empty bodies with `pass`. The other requirements in each description should remain intact.

The `pass` statements in the supplied code should remain where needed. These steps have no dedicated `pass` assertions to remove; their existing tests should remain unchanged.
